statusDetail: Completed audit of the UK HTTP 451 access-restriction surface. The underlying service and non-UK templates were not reachable from this region and are explicitly outside this run.

page.notes: The UK endpoint intentionally returns HTTP 451 and a single server-rendered legal restriction page.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Fixed dark colors are used with no preference query; computed color-scheme is normal.
Three animations remain running, including two infinite animations, when reduce is requested.
Forced colors maps body and heading to white on black and the link to yellow; all content remains visible.
The audited surface is a single static legal-restriction document with no route or state transition to animate.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited surface is a single static legal-restriction document with no route or state transition to animate.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The page has no scroll-linked effect, no scripts, and no scroll event handlers; it does not impose main-thread scroll motion.
There are no custom gesture handlers or gesture-driven controls; the only anchor retains platform-native interaction.
The restriction notice has no sticky or affixed chrome and no normal scroll journey requiring scroll-state feedback.
checkOutcomes.reason: The restriction notice has no sticky or affixed chrome and no normal scroll journey requiring scroll-state feedback.

checkOutcomes.method: Initial-load screenshot and DOM overlay inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: No popup, interstitial, consent banner, or overlay obscures the restriction message.

checkOutcomes.reason: The page has no modal, disclosure, picker, select, or transient overlay requiring a semantic dismissible primitive.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The viewport is almost entirely the short restriction message; there is no navigation or application chrome competing with it.
scrollWidth and innerWidth are both 360px; horizontal overflow is 0 and viewport metadata is present.
The sole card adapts intrinsically through max-width, percentage width, max-width on the image, and a narrow breakpoint; no reusable multi-container component exists.
The only interactive element is an inline text link, with a visible browser focus outline and no hover-only information.
The H1 immediately states Access Restricted and the next two paragraphs explain the UK restriction and why it exists.
The only available task in the audited region is understanding the legal restriction; the complete reason is visible without interaction or detours.
HTTP 451 accurately communicates legal unavailability and the page explains that UK access ended because age-verification requirements cannot be met.
Trace LCP is 1.62s, TBT 0ms with no long tasks; observed CLS is 0. The static page has no interaction workload.
The settled mobile load recorded CLS 0 with no shift entries.
Trace reports zero long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; the document ships no JavaScript.
Only three requests transfer 19,033 bytes, no render-blocking candidates are present, and cache-header hygiene is clear.
No JavaScript or external CSS ships; the complete page transfers about 19KB in three requests with no duplicate bundles.
The only image has alt text, the only control is a native anchor with text, and there are no form fields or canvas elements.

principleOutcomes.reason: All registered checks are inapplicable to this static legal-restriction surface.

paths.description: UK HTTP 451 restriction page: the only reachable template; exercised at desktop, mobile, preference, crawler and security/network conditions.
Short/zoom-equivalent viewport reflow stress case for the same restriction template.
Main content, listings, details, search, forms and account/commercial journeys were not covered because the audited UK region consistently receives the intentional legal HTTP 451 response.

findings.summary: The page hard-codes a dark palette rather than adapting to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS shows fixed #0d0d0d and #1a1a1a surfaces with no prefers-color-scheme rule; the emulated dark probe reports computed color-scheme "normal", so browser UI is not explicitly coordinated either.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare an appropriate color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens to offer a usable light variant while retaining the current dark design.

findings.summary: Infinite pulsing and glowing animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still reports fadeIn (1.2s), logoPulse (2.5s infinite), and glow (1.5s infinite) as running; no reduced-motion CSS exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to remove the entrance transform and disable the infinite logo and glow animations.

findings.summary: Short or highly zoomed viewports clip content and provide no way to scroll to it.
findings.evidence: At 320x300 the screenshot clips the top of the logo and bottom link; layout reports 327px of content in a 300px viewport while body uses height:100vh and overflow:hidden.
findings.suggestedFix: Use min-height:100dvh rather than fixed height, allow vertical overflow, and align to the top when content exceeds the viewport.

findings.summary: The small footer text is too dim against its dark card.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS sets 14px footer text to #777 on #1a1a1a, a contrast ratio of about 3.7:1, below WCAG AA’s 4.5:1 requirement for normal text; the desktop screenshot shows the low-emphasis text.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise the footer text color to at least approximately #929292 on #1a1a1a, and verify all states meet 4.5:1.

findings.summary: The restriction message has no main landmark.
findings.evidence: The semantic probe found one H1 but no main, header, nav, footer or aside landmark; the entire message is nested in generic div elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary restriction card in <main>; use <footer> for the closing note only if it represents page-level footer content.

findings.summary: The logo image does not declare intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image probe reports missing width and height attributes for the 335px-wide PNG. Measured CLS was 0 in this run, but intrinsic dimensions are still absent and can permit shifts under different cache/network timing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the logo’s intrinsic width and height attributes while retaining max-width:100%; optionally provide a compact WebP/AVIF alternative if it is smaller.

findings.summary: The public restriction response has no meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM and discoverability probes find title "Access Restricted" but no meta[name=description]; the message is otherwise fully server-rendered with 100% raw-content coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise description stating that PussySpace is unavailable in the United Kingdom because of age-verification requirements.

findings.summary: The HTTPS response lacks baseline content and transport security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS but reports no Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, or X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP for this static page, HSTS after confirming all subdomains support HTTPS, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.summary: The response provides no clickjacking, referrer, or permissions policy.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy, and no Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options as legacy coverage), strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, and a Permissions-Policy disabling unused capabilities.
